name: History Through Story
tagline: Every book is a door. Every door is a century.
subject: World History
description: A library exists outside of time. Each book on its shelves opens into a moment in history — you step through and you're there. Ancient Egypt, the Roman Forum, a Viking longship, the first flight at Kitty Hawk. Maren is the librarian. She doesn't tell you what happened. She puts the book in your hand and lets you see for yourself.

domains.name: The Ancient World
concepts: Ancient Egypt — pyramids, pharaohs, the Nile, hieroglyphics
Ancient Greece — democracy, philosophy, Olympics, mythology
Ancient Rome — republic to empire, engineering, law, daily life
Ancient China — dynasties, the Great Wall, invention, silk road
Mesopotamia — first cities, writing, Hammurabi's code
domains.mastery_signal: Can tell the story of each civilization in their own words, explain what made each one unique, and identify connections between them

domains.name: Castles & Caravans
concepts: Medieval Europe — feudalism, castles, knights, daily life
The Islamic Golden Age — science, math, medicine, architecture
Viking age — exploration, trade, mythology, shipbuilding
East Asia — Tang Dynasty, samurai Japan, Mongol Empire
The Silk Road — connecting civilizations through trade
domains.mastery_signal: Can explain how the medieval world was connected, describe daily life in different cultures, and identify what each contributed to the modern world

domains.name: The Modern World
concepts: Age of Exploration — Columbus, Magellan, the impact on indigenous peoples
Scientific Revolution — Galileo, Newton, the birth of modern science
Industrial Revolution — factories, steam, railroads, child labor
World Wars — causes, human cost, how they changed everything
Civil rights movements — people who changed the world by refusing to accept it
domains.mastery_signal: Can trace cause and effect across centuries, explain how inventions changed society, and identify the human cost of progress

domains.name: Thinking Like a Historian
concepts: Primary vs secondary sources — who wrote this and why
Perspective and bias — every story has a storyteller
Cause and effect — why did this happen, what happened next
Continuity and change — what stayed the same, what transformed
Making connections — patterns across time and place
domains.mastery_signal: Can look at a historical event, identify whose perspective is missing, and explain what the event means differently depending on who you ask

real_world_application: Understand where the modern world came from. Read the news and recognize historical patterns. Think critically about whose story is being told.
